summary: A specialty white tea from Satemwa Tea Estate in the Thyolo highlands of southern Malawi's Shire Highlands, made not from buds or leaves but from the tender new-growth stems of the tea plant, which dry into small forked shapes resembling antlers and give the tea its name. The stems carry a light coating of white down and, being lower in caffeine and higher in L-theanine than leaf material, yield an unusually mild, sweet cup with little bitterness. Satemwa is reported by specialty tea vendors to be the only estate producing this stem-based white tea, distinguishing it from the leaf teas typical of the wider white tea category.
